dimension_assessments.summary: The core specifies invocation, rendering, delivery, preview, and import behaviors across all three PlanUnits.
Teacher assistance, inline visualization, notification delivery, sound management, and compatibility import capabilities are enumerated.

Inputs include invocation phrases, visual markers, bridge methods, provider profiles, sound files, and manifests; outputs include rendered visualizers, disclosures, fallbacks, sends, receipts, previews, and imports.
Readiness, bridge, privacy, and media contracts exist, but quota/method, provider fixture, retry/idempotency, and media-limit details remain under-specified.
Teacher memory/degraded states, visualizer stream-to-final lifecycle, and notification retry/permanent outcomes are expressly included.
Explicit user action governs live external sends, while the compile is denied authority to create executable work artifacts.
Automated Testing owns the accepted validation criteria; implementation surfaces, dependencies, owner hints, and lineage are recorded.
Consumer-facing surfaces include Teacher threads/help/settings, inline visualizer webview/bridge adapters, and notification destinations and GUI previews.
All units are GUI-related and require concrete visible states, responsive/accessibility behavior, settings controls, fallbacks, previews, and feedback.
Missing-coverage, sandbox denial, retryable/permanent provider failure, and malformed imports are covered, but retry and idempotency recovery semantics are not testably bounded.
Source-backed Teacher answers, nonce validation, sandbox/network denial, payload redaction, no-secret evidence, and constrained live sends form explicit safety/privacy coverage.
Propagation paths include Teacher handoff, visualizer stream and native-adapter mapping, external provider delivery, and imported compatibility mapping.
Plan validation commands and future suite placeholders are named, but ATS-014 lacks a concrete executable behavioral test entrypoint and the future suites do not define receipt execution here.
Zero-flicker finalization and serialization are named, but no measurable load, concurrency, timing, resource, or queue thresholds are given.
Rust plus Slint adapter mapping and PeonPing/OpenPeon import compatibility are explicit, with unsupported/unknown import handling included.
Concrete behavioral assertions exist, but Teacher execution, visualizer quota/performance, notification retry/provider schemas, and sound limits lack complete pass/fail oracles.
Material discretion remains over test harnesses, quotas, bridge schemas, performance budgets, retry/idempotency, provider fixtures, receipts, and media limits.
The unresolved quantities and schemas are identifiable from the named-but-unbounded acceptance requirements and can lead to incompatible implementations.
